source_metadata.title: Circulating tumour DNA analysis to direct therapy in advanced breast cancer (plasmaMATCH): a multicentre, multicohort, phase 2a, platform trial
source_metadata.source_type: multicentre, multicohort, open-label, non-randomised phase 2a platform trial

batch_manifest.scope: study identity, design, eligibility, treatment cohorts, endpoints, statistical framework
ctDNA screening yield, turnaround, assay agreement, tissue concordance
ESR1 / extended-dose fulvestrant efficacy and safety
HER2 / neratinib plus conditional fulvestrant efficacy and safety
AKT1 ER-positive / capivasertib plus fulvestrant efficacy and safety
AKT1/PTEN cohort D, supplement timing method, limitation, conclusion

atoms.canonical_statement: The trial aimed to assess the clinical validity of ctDNA testing and whether ctDNA could select mutation-directed therapy in advanced breast cancer.
plasmaMATCH was a multicentre, open-label, non-randomised, multicohort phase 2a platform trial conducted across 18 UK hospitals.

Eligible participants were women aged at least 18 years with histologically confirmed advanced breast cancer, ECOG performance status 0-2, measurable disease, and prior treatment for advanced disease or early relapse after perioperative chemotherapy.

population.label: Eligible advanced breast cancer population
inclusion_criteria: prior advanced-disease treatment or relapse within 12 months of neoadjuvant/adjuvant chemotherapy

atoms.canonical_statement: Between 21 December 2016 and 26 April 2019, 1051 patients were registered for plasmaMATCH.
Cohort A treated patients with ESR1 mutations using extended-dose intramuscular fulvestrant 500 mg.
Cohort B treated HER2-mutant disease with oral neratinib 240 mg, adding standard-dose intramuscular fulvestrant when the cancer was oestrogen-receptor positive.
Cohort C treated AKT1-mutant, oestrogen-receptor-positive disease with oral capivasertib 400 mg plus standard-dose intramuscular fulvestrant.
Cohort D treated selected AKT1-mutant oestrogen-receptor-negative disease or PTEN-altered disease with oral capivasertib 480 mg.
The primary endpoint for each treatment cohort was confirmed objective response rate, assessed by RECIST version 1.1.

outcome.definition: confirmed complete or partial response by RECIST version 1.1

atoms.canonical_statement: Prespecified activity required at least 13 responses among 78 evaluable patients in cohort A and at least 3 responses among 16 evaluable patients in each of cohorts B, C, and D.
The platform used central droplet digital PCR and targeted ctDNA sequencing, with tissue sequencing used for retrospective comparison of mutation calls.
Radiological response assessment was scheduled every 8 weeks through week 32 and every 12 weeks thereafter.
Each treatment cohort used a single-stage A’Hern design with one-sided alpha 5% and 80% power.
The study was funded by Cancer Research UK, AstraZeneca, and Puma Biotechnology.
Among 1044 patients registered for ctDNA testing, 1034 received a ctDNA result (99.0%).
Digital PCR produced a result for 1025 of 1044 ctDNA-screening registrations (98.2%).
Targeted ctDNA sequencing results were available for 800 of 1044 ctDNA-screening registrations (76.6%).
Median turnaround time for digital PCR testing was 13 days (IQR 11-15).
Median turnaround time for targeted ctDNA sequencing was 10 days (IQR 8-11).
A mutation or amplification was identified in 533 of 1044 patients registered for ctDNA testing (51.1%).
A cohort-eligible target was identified in 357 of 1034 patients with ctDNA results (34.5%).
A total of 136 patients entered a treatment cohort through ctDNA testing.
Gene-level agreement between digital PCR and targeted ctDNA sequencing ranged from 96% to 99%.

population.label: Patients tested by both ctDNA methods

atoms.canonical_statement: Gene-level kappa values between digital PCR and targeted ctDNA sequencing ranged from 0.89 to 0.93.

population.label: Patients tested by both ctDNA methods

atoms.canonical_statement: Digital PCR ctDNA testing had 93% sensitivity (95% CI 83-98) for mutations identified by advanced-disease tissue sequencing.
For contemporaneous tissue biopsies, digital PCR ctDNA sensitivity was 98% (95% CI 87-100).
For time-discordant tissue samples, digital PCR ctDNA sensitivity was 85% (95% CI 66-96).
Targeted ctDNA sequencing had 95% sensitivity (95% CI 87-99) for mutations identified by advanced-disease tissue sequencing.
For contemporaneous tissue biopsies, targeted ctDNA sequencing sensitivity was 100% (95% CI 92-100).
Cohort A enrolled 84 patients with ESR1-mutant disease; 74 were evaluable for the primary response endpoint.
Cohort A had 6 confirmed partial responses among 74 evaluable patients, an objective response rate of 8% (95% CI 3-17).
Median duration of response in cohort A was 7.0 months (IQR 3.7-8.3).
Clinical benefit occurred in 12 of 74 evaluable cohort A patients (16%, 95% CI 9-27).
Median progression-free survival in cohort A was 2.2 months (95% CI 1.8-3.6).
Among patients with clonally dominant ESR1 mutations in cohort A, 5 of 41 responded (12%, 95% CI 4-26).

population.label: Cohort A clonally dominant ESR1 subgroup

atoms.canonical_statement: Among patients with subclonal ESR1 mutations in cohort A, none of 27 responded (0%, 95% CI 0-13).
Raised gamma-glutamyltransferase was the most common grade 3-4 adverse event in cohort A, occurring in 13 of 80 treated patients (16%).
One serious adverse reaction, grade 3 superior sagittal sinus thrombosis, occurred in cohort A.

concept.text: serious adverse reaction: superior sagittal sinus thrombosis

atoms.canonical_statement: Cohort A did not reach its prespecified activity threshold.
Cohort B enrolled 21 patients with HER2-mutant disease; 20 were evaluable for the primary response endpoint.
Cohort B had 5 confirmed responses among 20 evaluable patients, an objective response rate of 25% (95% CI 9-49).
Median duration of response in cohort B was 5.7 months (IQR 3.7-9.7).
Clinical benefit occurred in 9 of 20 evaluable cohort B patients (45%, 95% CI 23-68).
Median progression-free survival in cohort B was 5.4 months (95% CI 3.4-9.1).
Grade 3-4 diarrhoea occurred in 4 of 20 cohort B patients (20%) according to the main Results and Supplementary Table S5.
Grade 3-4 hypertension occurred in 3 of 20 cohort B patients (15%).
Cohort B met or exceeded its prespecified activity threshold, and one complete response was ongoing at 29 months at data cutoff.
Cohort C enrolled 18 patients with AKT1-mutant, oestrogen-receptor-positive disease; all 18 were evaluable.
Cohort C had 4 confirmed partial responses among 18 evaluable patients, an objective response rate of 22% (95% CI 6-48).
Median duration of response in cohort C was 7.5 months (IQR 4.1-9.8).
Clinical benefit occurred in 7 of 18 cohort C patients (39%, 95% CI 17-64).
Median progression-free survival in cohort C was 10.2 months (95% CI 3.2-18.2).
Grade 3-4 fatigue occurred in 4 of 18 cohort C patients (22%).
Grade 3-4 rash occurred in 3 of 18 cohort C patients (17%).
One treatment-related death caused by grade 4 dyspnoea occurred in cohort C.
Cohort D enrolled 19 patients: 6 had AKT1 mutations and 13 had PTEN alterations; all 19 were evaluable.
Cohort D had 2 confirmed partial responses among 19 evaluable patients, an objective response rate of 11% (95% CI 1-33).
Median duration of response in cohort D was 3.9 months (IQR 3.7-4.2).
Clinical benefit occurred in 2 of 19 cohort D patients (11%).
Median progression-free survival in cohort D was 3.4 months (95% CI 1.8-5.5).
Among the 6 cohort D patients with AKT1 mutations, 2 responded (33%, 95% CI 4-78).
None of the 13 cohort D patients with PTEN alterations had a confirmed response.
Grade 3-4 rash occurred in 5 of 19 cohort D patients (26%).
A tissue biopsy was defined as contemporaneous when less than 60 days elapsed between tissue biopsy and plasma sampling for ctDNA analysis.
The authors noted that the treatment cohorts included relatively heavily pretreated patients, which could reduce apparent treatment activity, particularly in cohort A.

The authors concluded that ctDNA testing provided accurate, rapid genotyping suitable for selecting mutation-directed therapies and that HER2- and AKT1-directed cohorts showed clinically relevant activity.
